translation.title: Azelaic Acid Cream
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for acne vulgaris (common acne).
translation.usage: Before applying this medicine, wash the affected area clean with clean water or a mild cleanser and dry it, then — unless directed otherwise by a doctor or pharmacist — apply a sufficient amount to the affected area twice a day (morning and evening) and rub it in well. The treatment period varies from person to person and with the severity of the acne, but a clear treatment effect generally appears after about 4 weeks; for the best results, use it regularly and consistently for several months. If skin irritation is very severe, reduce use to once a day until the irritation goes away, or consult a doctor or pharmacist.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it. Before using it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, for children under 12, or if you are or have been hypersensitive to propylene glycol. Use it without skipping during the treatment period. Do not use an occlusive dressing or wrapping. This medicine is for external use only. Be careful not to let it touch the eyes, nose, mouth or other mucous membranes, and if it gets into the eyes, rinse them out completely with plenty of water. Always wash the hands you used to apply the medicine with water. Stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist if adverse reactions occur, such as sensitivity, severe irritation, very commonly a burning feeling, itching or redness at the application site, commonly peeling, pain, dryness, discoloration or irritation at the application site, uncommonly oiliness, acne, skin depigmentation, abnormal sensations at the application site, dermatitis, discomfort or swelling, rarely small depigmented spots, excessive hair growth, flushing (a sign of keratosis pilaris), cheilitis and worsening of recurrent cold sores, drug hypersensitivity reactions, small blisters at the application site, eczema, fever or ulcers, and with unknown frequency angioedema, contact dermatitis, eye swelling, a swollen face (which may accompany a hypersensitivity reaction), a rash, hives or worsening of asthma. Flushing, scaling, itching, a burning feeling and hypopigmentation (an abnormal change in skin color in people with darker skin) may also occur.
